messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2701 opened by monitoring — Latency SLO breach detected in live for streaming endpoints (p99 spike).

maria: seeing big p99 jump across a subset of replicas, p95 up ~2x. customers reporting intermittent stalls on long streams. assigning oncall.

alex: currently looking at prefix-cache hit rate — just noticed a rollout 10m ago that changed prefix-hash salt for prefixcache v2. hit rate dropped from 92% -> 18% on affected shards. suspicious.

kai: confirm. routing logs show elevated KV miss rate and more paging. stream stalls correlate with cache-miss spikes on kvbucket-14.

jess: impacted customers flagged via alerting: two high-usage tenants, one started a support ticket about repeated stalled completions. potential customer impact.

maria: quick customer impact summary for pager duty: P95 degraded from ~120ms to ~380ms, P99 from ~1.3s to ~5.1s for streaming produce/consume. error-rate normal, just latency/timeouts on stalls.

alex: dumping small diagnostic:
```
# top prefixes by hit rate delta
prefixcache.v2.kvbucket-14: hit_rate_before=0.92 hit_rate_now=0.18
prefixcache.v2.kvbucket-21: hit_rate_before=0.90 hit_rate_now=0.88
affected_shards=[14,17]
rollout_change="prefix-hash-salt=v2.3.1"
```

kai: also seeing continuous batching queue length increase on those shards, and tail latency on streaming websocket send. stack traces show repeated backend fetches for the same prefixes.

maria: root cause hypothesis: prefix-hash salt change caused cache key churn -> massive cold misses -> paging -> increased downstream tail latencies for streaming sessions.

jess: did we have a canary? what rollout policy applied?

deploy-bot: deploy 2701239900 by ops/batch-rollouts completed 10 minutes ago, policy=gradual-25pc-5m.

alex: looks like canary windows were too small for prefix keyspace; the salt change is non-backwards compatible so cacheable entries invalidated on all serving nodes as they reconcile.

maria: mitigation plan (short term): 1) pause further rollout 2) rollback salt to previous value on serving config 3) enable aggressive prefix warmup from origin for affected shards 4) temporary routing to older model variant for heavy customers if needed.

kai: executing rollback on config. command: `redwoodctl config set prefixcache.salt v2.3.0 --env=prod --target=kvbucket-14,17 --no-wait`

alex: warming scripts ready. will run a controlled warmup: `scripts/prefix_warmup.sh --shard 14,17 --rate 2000/s --keys-file suspect-prefixes.txt`

maria: set SLO notice and customer comms. jess please draft an initial status update to affected customers.

jess: on it — short note: we detected increased latency stemming from a cache rollout, mitigation in progress, expected recovery within 20-40 minutes after rollback and warmup. will update if we see regression.

deploy-bot: rollback job 2701240101 started by maria.

alex: after rollback triggered: watching hit rate metrics. initial replication of config rollback looks successful on kvbucket-14 replicas.

sre-bot: metric alert cleared for p95 on region-us-west after 12m of rollback/warmup but p99 still elevated by ~600ms.

kai: digging tail traces — some long-lived streaming sessions keep stalled due to client-side backpressure + KV time to rebuild range. those sessions will recover once KV cache warms.

maria: action items: alex keep warming until hit_rate > 85% on shards 14/17. kai monitor stream queue and drop stalled sessions if exceeding threshold to free resources. jess coordinate customer updates. I'll keep the oncall handoff if this persists.

alex: warming script completed first pass. hit_rate now 63% -> continuing incremental warmup.

jess: update sent to customers at 14:18 PT, included rollback and ETA. reactions: :thumbsup: :heart: from a couple customers.

maria: status update for timeline:
- 2701239999 root alert: p99 jump detected
- 2701239900 rollout that changed prefix-hash salt
- 2701240101 rollback started
- 2701240400 warmup ongoing, partial recovery
- 2701240700 p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~1.0s (improving)

alex: follow-up diagnostics to run after incident: compare pre/post prefix distribution, add automated canary that fails rollout if global hit_rate delta > 10% within 15m, and add a non-destructive migration path for salt changes (dual-keying).

kai: ops note: for future salt changes we should seed new keys into cache via background replication before switching the serving salt — avoids mass invalidation.

maria: oncall handoff plan: I'll remain oncall until we hit stable p99 < 700ms for 30m or until 15:00 PT, whichever is later. handoff to next oncall @alex if not recovered.

jess: will track support ticket and summary for postmortem.

maria: closing live mitigation. moving to postmortem and action items channel. thanks all for quick response. :raised_hands:

inc-bot: INCIDENT 2701 severity=sev2 -> monitoring continues; postmortem required.
